title: "Patterns by Ear"

No notes on a staff here: patterns are learned from the keys and by listening.
The first few patterns of a set are taught with finger numbers on an on-screen keyboard. Then the page plays the rest, one at a time,
and you play each back on your keyboard.

```{=html}
<div class="ep-panel">
  <div class="ep-dots" id="ep-dots2"></div>
  <div class="ep-head" id="ep-ear-head">Learn the first patterns, then come here.</div>
  <div class="ep-solf" id="ep-ear-solf"></div>
  <div class="ep-kb" id="ep-kb-ear"></div>
  <div class="ep-msg" id="ep-ear-msg" aria-live="polite"></div>

    <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary" id="ep-ear-key">Hear the key</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary" id="ep-ear-show">Show me</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary" id="ep-ear-skip">Skip</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary" id="ep-ear-next" hidden>Next ▶</button>
  </div>
  <p class="ep-muted">The key is played first (I – V7 – I). Then each pattern: listen, then play it back. A wrong note stops the

</div>
```

## How it works {#how}

- **The sets.** The same sets as Tonal Patterns: the stepwise and I–V sets, the 322–324 sets, and any set you make there.
  The first patterns of a set use the same chords as the rest, so learning them gives you the sound of each chord before you're tested.
- **Fingering.** The page works out the fingers itself. It keeps the hand in one position (no thumb-under, as these patterns are short),
  goes with the letter steps (C E G is 1 3 5), and keeps the thumb off black keys where it can. This is a rule of thumb, not taken
  from a method book: a teacher may prefer other fingers.
- **What counts.** The notes in order. Rhythm and fingers are not checked. With *Any octave counts* on, the whole pattern may be an
  octave up or down. Stopping for more than four seconds starts the try again.
- **No MIDI keyboard?** The computer keys play notes (bottom row white keys from Z = middle C, the row above black keys; ↑ ↓ change octave).
